messages.subject: Re: "Can't find object" when rewriting correct code into function
parts:
Hi

On Sun, Mar 10, 2013 at 6:41 PM, Ric_Ren <richard...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I am really confused to see it happening:
>
> The dataset is like this:
>> names(DF1)
> [1] "height" "fert" "interval" "cwt"
>
> Firstly, when I write the code with ggplot it gives correct results:
> ggplot(DF1,aes(x=fert,y=cwt,
> shape=factor(interval) ))+
> labs(x="fert",y="cwt",shape="interval")+
> geom_point()+geom_line()+
> facet_wrap(as.formula(~height))
> ##which plots an interaction plot of the 3 factors: fert, interval, height,
> facet_wrapped by heights.
>
> (1)Since I need to reuse the code multiple times, I adapt it into a function
> and that is when things start to turn ridiculous:
> plot.interactions<-function(DF, xname, yname, groupname, facetname){
> p<-ggplot(data=DF, aes(x=DF[,xname],
> y=DF[,yname],shape=factor(DF[,groupname])))+
> labs(x=xname,y=yname,shape=groupname)+
> geom_point()+geom_line()+
> facet_wrap(as.formula(paste0("~",facetname)))
> return(p)
> }
> ##Error: cannot find the object DF. (what???I just passed that into the
> function!!!)

This has to do with the environment aes looks in I think.

>
> (2) I also tried using "aes_string" instead of "aes".

This is the correct approach: aes_string was written for exactly this
purpose (i.e., so you don't have to mess around with the environment
issue with aes() ).

The error above is
> gone but has grouping (in "shape") issues: Continuous value supplied to
> discrete scale.

In you function to the factor conversions before plotting.

>
> I think ggplot2 function is somehow flawed because when I adapt a correct
> code into a function, it should give same result.

Everything is flawed in some way I suppose, but the ggplot2 developers
anticipated your problem and helpfully wrote aes_string.

>
> Do you guys know why the "can't find object " mistake happens? Is there a
> way to adapt the code into a function that gives the correct result?

You did not give us a reproducible example, so it's hard to know if
this solves all your problems. But here is an example using mtcars
that does what you describe:

plot.interactions<-function(DF, xname, yname, groupname, facetname){
DF[[groupname]] <- factor(groupname)
p<-ggplot(data=DF, aes_string(x=xname, y=yname,shape=groupname))+
geom_point()+geom_line()+
facet_wrap(as.formula(paste0("~",facetname)))
return(p)
}

plot.interactions(DF=mtcars, xname="hp", yname="mpg", groupname="vs",
facetname="am")

Finally, note that this already exists as the qplot function:

qplot(x=hp, y=mpg, shape=factor(vs), geom=c("point", "line"),
facets=~am, data=mtcars)

Best,
Ista
